newsitem.title: USA: Stock market romps to yet another record high.
newsitem.headline: Stock market romps to yet another record high.

text.p: Stocks romped to record highs for the second session in a row Tuesday, lifting the Dow Jones industrial average within a few points of a new milestone of 7,400 points following a powerful rally in technology shares.
The Dow ended up 37.50 points at 7,383.41, beating Friday's record finish of 7,345.91. The market was closed Monday for Memorial Day.
The blue-chip index at one time surged to 7,394.95, just short of the 7,400 level.
But in the broader market, declining issues outnumbered advances 1,299 to 1,222 on active volume of 435 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq Composite and the Standard & Poor's 500 indices also set second consecutive highs.

The Dow was on a roll, racing back from an early loss of nearly 40 points as it tracked the rise in International Business Machines Corp., which surged 5-1/2 to a new all-time high of 178-7/8, one day before IBM's much-anticipated two-for-one stock split.
It was the second record high in less than five trading sessions for IBM after last Wednesday's 175-1/8 -- its first record close since August, 1987.
Analysts said the rally in technology stocks was rooted in positive comments on Micron Technology Inc. by an influential analyst. Micron jumped 4-3/8 to 42-5/8.
Merrill Lynch's Tom Kurlak, a long-time bull, said he expected Micron to earn even more in 1997 and 1998 than he previously expected.

"All the action was in technology today. It's contagious," said Kenneth Ducey, director of trading at BT Securities. "When you like one (tech stock), you like the group, both first and second tier. That's the momentum that got things going."

The rally touched almost every sector of the technology group, from computer companies to chip stocks to networking firms. Even disk drive makers rebounded, recovering slightly from recent losses that were driven by fears that disk drive prices would drop further.
"People are coming to their senses. These things tend to get overdone. They get oversold and then they come back," said Brian Finnerty, senior vice president at Unterberg Harris.
"Basically, inflation is slow. Earnings have been great. It's just a great environment for tech stocks," he said.
The stock market broke away from the downdraft in bonds, where the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond fell 15/32, which raised its yield to 7.03 percent from Friday's close of 6.99 percent.
The inflation-sensitive bond traders sold on news that the Conference Board's index of U.S. consumer confidence hit a 28-year high of 127.1 in May, vs. a reading of 118.5 in April.
The upbeat data sparked concern that the high level of confidence among consumers might lead to brisker spending, which could provoke the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates later this summer.
The jump in the bond's yield above 7 percent fuelled some early selling in stocks, since it is the level at which many money managers switch funds into bonds.
"That's the magic number that makes a lot of people nervous but people are still following the momentum, and it is strong, until it shows signs of slowing," Ducey said.
AT&T Corp., another Dow component, rose 1-3/8 to 37-1/2 on a report that the telecommunications giant might merge with local phone company SBC Communications Corp. SBC rose 3/4 to 57-5/8.
The world's largest chipmaker, Intel Corp., jumped 6-1/8 to 169-5/16. 3Com Corp. rose 3-1/2 to 46-3/4 Dell Computer rose 6 to 113-1/4.
Bank stocks could not escape the weakness in the bond market. Citicorp fell 4-5/8 to 113-1/4, BankAmerica Corp. lost 3-1/2 to 114-1/8 and J.P Morgan & Co. slid 1-3/8 to 103-3/8.
The Nasdaq Composite index rose 19.49 points to a new high of 1,409.21.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks was up 2.68 to 849.71, a new high. The American Stock Exchange index edged up 0.50 to 598.44.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks rose 0.39 to 440.67, a new high. The average share was up 4 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was at a new high 8,026.597 up 26.276 or 0.33 percent.
